    Without Compose, run node utils/web-console/backup_worker.mjs bundle-restore --bundle <ID> --mode stage. The bundle IDs are on the Server state tab of a console that still sees the destination, or in the destination under server/. The command prints the staging directory:

    text
    bundle_restore <operation ID>: succeeded, staged in <BUNDLE_STAGING_DIR>/<time>-<ID>

    The directory, readable by its owner only, holds the files under their original paths and a RESTORE.txt. Stop the server, copy the staged configuration into place, restore the owners and modes of the files, and start the server.

  3. Restore Keeper, if the bundle includes a Keeper snapshot: stop Keeper, move its snapshots and logs aside, put the staged snapshot into its snapshot directory, and start it.

  4. Restore the databases. In the console:

    1. On Administration → Backup & Restore, select Set up if the page offers it.
    2. On Destinations, add the destinations again with the same names, then test and enable them.
    3. For the latest backup of each database, select Restore…. In Names and options, replace the suggested target restore_<database>_<time> with the database's own name. Select Also restore the access entities, and Also restore the functions, workloads, and resources, when the backup contains them. On Confirm, type the target name and select Start restore.

    The restore fails on existing objects instead of adding data to them: on a new server, the databases and access entities do not exist yet.

  5. Check. On Server state, select Compare on the bundle: every file should be the same as on the host. Then run a restore test of the latest backups: Test restore on their rows in Backups.

  6. Clean up. Delete the staging directory: it holds secrets in clear.

Rehearse the recovery

utils/web-console/recovery_rehearsal.mjs proves the procedure without touching production. It:

  • starts an isolated server that listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on its own ports, with its own data directory and its own embedded Keeper;
  • with --staged, starts it from the staged configuration of a server bundle, with its storage, Keeper, clusters, and paths replaced, so that it can never write to production; this checks that the configuration of the bundle starts;
  • restores each backup from its real destination, which it only reads, into the rehearsal server's own disk;
  • compares every table that has recorded values: row count and fingerprint (groupBitXor(cityHash64(*)));
  • records the result with each backup, shown as Recovery rehearsed (or Rehearsal failed) in the inventory, and in the audit log, then stops the rehearsal server and removes its directory.

Production is read (destinations, backups, and the values recorded when they were made) and receives only the result.

  1. Choose the host. Run the rehearsal on the server host, or a host that mounts the backups: a disk destination is read from its path on this host. It needs Node.js 18 or later and a clickhouse binary.

  2. Prepare the account and the credentials. The user needs SELECT on the console tables and INSERT on backup_events and audit_log. For S3 destinations, export the worker's credentials: <REF>_ACCESS_KEY_ID and <REF>_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

  3. Optional: stage a bundle. Select Stage… on the latest bundle on Server state, or run bundle-restore --mode stage. --staged needs a bundle that includes /etc/clickhouse-server (the default of BUNDLE_PATHS).

  4. Run it, for example monthly:

    bash
    node utils/web-console/recovery_rehearsal.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:8123 --user <admin> --password <password> \
    --binary /usr/bin/clickhouse [--staged <staging directory of a server bundle>]
    ArgumentMeaning
    --url, --user, --passwordThe production server and its account (default CLICKHOUSE_URL, CLICKHOUSE_USER, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, then http://127.0.0.1:8123 and default).
    --backup <operation ID>A backup to rehearse; repeat for several. Default: the latest successful backup of each database.
    --staged <directory>The staging directory of a server bundle, to start from its configuration.
    --binary <path>The clickhouse binary (default clickhouse).
    --work-dir <directory>The directory of the rehearsal server (default tmp/recovery-rehearsal-<time> in the current directory).
    --keepKeep the work directory after the rehearsal.

    The ports are chosen free by the system, or set with REHEARSAL_HTTP_PORT, REHEARSAL_TCP_PORT, REHEARSAL_KEEPER_PORT, and REHEARSAL_RAFT_PORT. ADMIN_DATABASE names the database of the console tables (default console_admin).

Verify

The rehearsal prints a line per backup, then a summary, and exits with code 0 only when every backup was restored and matched:

text
Recovery rehearsal: 2 of 2 backups restored and matched

In the console, the backups show Recovery rehearsed; its tooltip names the time and whether the staged configuration was used. The audit log has a recovery_rehearsal record.

Troubleshooting

MessageCause and fix
There is no successful backup to rehearse.No successful backup with an existing destination is recorded. Make a backup first.
No successful backup <ID> with an existing destination.The ID given with --backup is not a successful backup, or its destination was removed.
The backups of the disk <name> are not readable here (<path>): run the rehearsal on the server host.Run it where the disk's path exists.
Set <REF>_ACCESS_KEY_ID and _SECRET_ACCESS_KEY to read the destination <name>.Export the worker's credentials of that S3 destination.
<directory>/config.xml does not exist: --staged is the staging directory of a server bundle that includes /etc/clickhouse-server.Stage a bundle that includes /etc/clickhouse-server, or omit --staged.
The rehearsal server did not start with the staged configuration: …The configuration of the bundle does not start: fix it before you need it. --keep keeps server.log and server.err.log in the work directory.
No server bundle <ID>: give --bundle <operation ID>.The worker's server has no record of the bundle: see the note under Prerequisites.
The bundle was encrypted with the master key …; this worker has ….Use the key the bundle was made with.

For the restore itself, see Restores; for the helper processes, Helper processes.

how-to/build-and-package-images.title: Build and package the Docker images
how-to/build-and-package-images.description: Build the server image and the tools image of the web console from source, and package them as archives for distribution, with build_images.sh and package_images.sh.
how-to/build-and-package-images.html:
Build the two Docker images of the web console from the repository, smoke-test them, and package them as archives that can be copied to any environment, including networks without access to a registry.

ImageContents
clickhouse-server-console:<version>The official clickhouse/clickhouse-server image of the same release, with the clickhouse binary of this build (utils/web-console/Dockerfile). Everything of the official image applies: its environment variables, config.d, users.d, and docker-entrypoint-initdb.d.
clickhouse-console-tools:<version>Node.js 22 with the helper processes, console.html for the access policy worker, the docker CLI with Compose, and kubectl (utils/web-console/Dockerfile.tools). See Tools image.

The version is <tag of the base image>-console.<commit>, with an 11-character commit hash, for example 26.9.8.3-console.a88866202a2, and the suffix -dirty when uncommitted changes were allowed.

Prerequisites

  • A clone of the repository, with your changes committed. The scripts refuse uncommitted changes in programs/, src/, or utils/web-console/, because the version would not identify what the images contain.
  • Docker, running and usable by your user, and Git.
  • To build the binary: CMake, Ninja, and Clang. The script uses CC and CXX when they are set, otherwise clang-22 and clang++-22 when installed, otherwise clang and clang++.
  • About 60 GB free in the build directory.
  • For --with-rust only: rustup with the toolchain named in contrib/corrosion-cmake/CMakeLists.txt.
  • The official server image of the same release as the binary, by default clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.9.8.3. The script pulls it when it is not on the host.

Steps

  1. Build the images from source

    Run from the repository root:

    bash
    utils/web-console/build_images.sh

    The script runs four steps:

    1. Checks: the tools, Docker, the free space, and uncommitted changes. Everything that would otherwise fail after hours of compiling is checked first.
    2. Configure a Release build in build_release/, once, with -DENABLE_TESTS=0 and -DENABLE_RUST=OFF (or ON with --with-rust). The output is in build_release/cmake.log. An existing build directory must be a Release build with the same Rust choice, or the script stops.
    3. Build the clickhouse binary with Ninja, with the output in build_release/ninja_release.log. The first build takes several hours (about 6 on 22 cores); later builds compile only what changed. An interrupted build resumes where it stopped when you run the script again.
    4. Package the images with package_images.sh (a few minutes).

    To follow the build from another terminal:

    bash
    tail -c 300 build_release/ninja_release.log | tr '\r' '\n' | grep -o '\[[0-9]*/[0-9]*\]' | tail -1

  2. Or package an existing binary

    To package a binary that is already built, without building:

    bash
    utils/web-console/build_images.sh --package-only

    or call package_images.sh directly with any Release or RelWithDebInfo binary:

    bash
    utils/web-console/package_images.sh --binary build_release/programs/clickhouse

  3. Find the archives

    The output directory, by default tmp/dist/<version>/ in the repository, contains:

    FileContents
    clickhouse-server-console-<version>-amd64.tar.gzThe server image, to load with docker load -i.
    clickhouse-console-tools-<version>-amd64.tar.gzThe tools image, to load with docker load -i.
    MANIFEST.txtThe version, the commit, the build time, the platform (linux/amd64), the base image digest, the server binary version and build type, the image IDs, and the commands to load, verify, and deploy.
    SHA256SUMSChecksums of the two archives and MANIFEST.txt.
    deploy/A copy of utils/web-console/deploy/: the Docker Compose files, kubernetes.yaml, .env.example, config.d/, service-accounts.sql, and README.md, the guide for the operators of each environment. CONSOLE_VERSION in .env.example and the image tags in kubernetes.yaml are set to this version.

Options of build_images.sh

OptionMeaning
--build-dir <dir>Build directory. Default: build_release in the repository.
--with-rustAlso build the Rust components: the PRQL dialect, fuzzy history search in clickhouse-client (skim), WebAssembly UDFs (wasmtime), and polyglot. Default: without them.
--package-onlyDo not build: package the binary already in the build directory.
--base-image <image>The official server image of the same release. Default: that of package_images.sh, clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.9.8.3.
--out <dir>Output directory. Default: tmp/dist/<version>.
--allow-dirtyAllow uncommitted changes; the version gets the suffix -dirty.
-h, --helpPrint the usage.

Options of package_images.sh

OptionMeaning
--binary <path>The clickhouse binary. Default: build_release/programs/clickhouse.
--base-image <image>The official server image of the same release. Default: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.9.8.3.
--out <dir>Output directory. Default: tmp/dist/<version>.
--allow-dirtyAllow uncommitted changes; the version gets the suffix -dirty.

package_images.sh:

  1. refuses a binary whose CMakeCache.txt is not a Release or RelWithDebInfo build, and a binary whose release differs from the tag of the base image;
  2. strips the debug information of the binary (llvm-strip-22 --strip-debug, or strip --strip-debug); the symbols stay, so that stack traces in the server log keep their function names;
  3. builds both images with the labels org.opencontainers.image.version and org.opencontainers.image.revision;
  4. smoke-tests them, then saves them with docker save and gzip.

Verify

The script prints MANIFEST.txt and the content of the output directory at the end. Before it saves the images, it checks that:

  • the server image starts, reports the release of the binary (SELECT version()), answers 200 on /console, and serves the page of this build;
  • each of backup-worker, cluster-agent, and access-policy-worker starts in the tools image and fails only on the connection to a server, not on a syntax error or a missing module or file;
  • docker, docker compose, kubectl, and node are present in the tools image.

On the target host, verify the archives and load them:

bash
cd tmp/dist/<version>
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
docker load -i clickhouse-server-console-<version>-amd64.tar.gz
docker load -i clickhouse-console-tools-<version>-amd64.tar.gz
docker run --rm clickhouse-console-tools:<version> version

Then deploy with Docker Compose or Kubernetes.

Troubleshooting

MessageCause and fix
the working tree has uncommitted changes in programs/, src/, or utils/web-console/Commit the changes, or pass --allow-dirty.
Docker is not running, or this user cannot use itStart Docker, or add your user to the group that may use its socket.
only <n> GB free in <dir>; the build needs about 60 GBFree space, or choose another --build-dir. The check is skipped when the binary is already built.
<dir> is a <type> build: use another --build-dirThe build directory is not a Release build: a Debug binary is several gigabytes and slow. Use another directory.
<dir> was configured with ENABLE_RUST=<value>The Rust choice differs from the configured one: use another --build-dir, or add or remove --with-rust.
--with-rust needs the Rust toolchain <toolchain>Install it with rustup toolchain install <toolchain>.
the build failed; the full output is in <dir>/ninja_release.logThe script prints the first errors. Fix them and run the script again: the build resumes.
the binary comes from a <type> buildpackage_images.sh packages only Release or RelWithDebInfo builds.
the binary is version <x>, the base image <y>Pass the official image of the binary's release with --base-image.
/console answered: ... or /console does not serve the page of this buildThe binary is not a build with the console: check that the binary is the one you built.
<process> does not start: ...A helper process of the tools image has a syntax error or a missing file.

how-to/run-browser-checks.title: Run the browser acceptance checks
how-to/run-browser-checks.description: Run the browser acceptance suites of the web console with run_e2e.sh, against a server, MinIO, cluster agent, OpenLDAP, and Keycloak started for the run.
how-to/run-browser-checks.html:
Run the browser acceptance suites of the web console with utils/web-console/run_e2e.sh. Every run starts from nothing: a new server with an empty data directory, and its own MinIO, cluster agent, Vault, OpenLDAP, Keycloak, and token authenticator as the suites need them, which it stops and removes at the end. The results depend only on the code, not on what a person or an earlier run left on a server, and no other server on the machine is touched.

Prerequisites

  • A clickhouse binary built from the repository, by default build/programs/clickhouse. With --page-from-source, the page comes from the working tree instead of the binary.

  • Node.js (node).

  • A Playwright workspace outside of the repository, by default ~/console-e2e, with node_modules/playwright and Chromium. Playwright is a development tool only:

    bash
    mkdir -p ~/console-e2e && cd ~/console-e2e
npm init -y && npm install playwright@1.48.2 && npx playwright install chromium
# If Chromium reports missing libraries: sudo npx playwright install-deps chromium

  • curl, ss, and, for the ldap suite, openssl.

  • For the backup, cluster, ldap, and sso suites: Docker, running and usable by your user.

  • These images on the host (the script does not pull them):

    SuiteImage
    backupminio/minio:RELEASE.2025-07-23T15-54-02Z
    backup (optional)hashicorp/vault:1.17.6: without it, the bundle checks use a stand-in of its API
    clusterclickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.9.8.3 and contentsquareplatform/chproxy:v1.30.0, for the lab clusters
    ldapbitnamilegacy/openldap:2.6.8
    ssoquay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7
    bash
    docker pull minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-07-23T15-54-02Z
docker pull bitnamilegacy/openldap:2.6.8
docker pull quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7

  • The ports free.

Steps

  1. Run the suites

    From the repository root:

    bash
    utils/web-console/run_e2e.sh                                    # all suites, with the page built into the binary
utils/web-console/run_e2e.sh --page-from-source                 # with programs/server/console.html as it is now
utils/web-console/run_e2e.sh --suites console,access            # only some suites

    The script prints, for each suite, Running <suite> and then the last line of its log with its exit status.

  2. Read the result

    The script ends with All suites passed and exit code 0, or with Failed: followed by the failed suites and exit code 1. Open the log of a failed suite in tmp/console-e2e-run/logs/ (see Logs).

  3. Inspect what a suite left, if needed

    With --keep, the server, MinIO, and the cluster agent stay running at the end, and the script prints the address of the server (http://127.0.0.1:38123, user default). Stop them before the next run: a run refuses to start while its ports are in use.

Options

OptionMeaning
--suites <list>Suites to run, separated by commas: console, access, data_access, backup, cluster, ldap, sso. Default: all of them. An unknown name is refused.
--binary <path>The clickhouse binary. Default: build/programs/clickhouse.
--page-from-sourceServe programs/server/console.html from the working tree, instead of the page built into the binary, with the headers of the built-in handler: try a change of the page without rebuilding. The other pages and /console/config.json come from the binary.
--e2e-dir <dir>The Playwright workspace with node_modules/playwright. Default: ~/console-e2e.
--keepLeave the server, MinIO, and the agent running at the end, for inspection.
-h, --helpPrint the usage.

Suites

The suites run in this order:

SuiteScriptWhat it checksWhat it starts
consoleconsole_e2e.mjsThe console: sign-in, home page, panels, routes, and the restrictions of a limited user (limited, without SELECT ON system.part_log and INTROSPECTION).The server
accessaccess_e2e.mjsThe Administration pages, including a partly applied ON CLUSTER change on the cluster console_test, whose second shard is a port where nothing listens.The server
data_accessdata_access_e2e.mjsData Access Policies with synthetic users and data, over HTTP and with the native client, including the access policy worker; the clusters dap_secret (with an interserver secret) and console_test.The server
backupserver_bundle_test.mjs, then backup_e2e.mjsThe server bundle module alone (bundle_module), then Backup & Restore, including server bundles with a key file, a server restart (kill -9 of the server and its watchdog), and an unavailable destination (MinIO stopped and started).MinIO with the bucket ch-backups; Vault with a Transit key when its image is present
clustercluster_e2e.mjsCluster Management against a running agent: provisioning, registration (with the credential reference PLATFORM), drift, scaling, failures, and retirement. It creates Docker lab clusters e2e-* and deletes them.The cluster agent
ssosso_e2e.mjsIdentity Providers → SSO (Keycloak), the test sign-in, and signing in to the console with Keycloak: the token refresh, a user without a ClickHouse user, sign-out, and a user disabled in Keycloak.Keycloak with the realm clickhouse; the token authenticator with its user sync
ldapldap_e2e.mjsDirectory sign-in: the generated LDAP configuration installed on the server, sign-in with roles from groups, directory changes, and users managed with SQL next to the directory. It restarts the server and removes the directory at the end, so it runs last.OpenLDAP with LDAPS and a certificate authority of the run

The server is configured with an embedded Keeper, the clusters console_test, dap_nosecret, and dap_secret, a disk backups allowed in backups.allowed_disk, remote_url_allow_hosts for 127.0.0.1 and localhost, and web_console.backup_s3_endpoints with the MinIO endpoint and the patterns https://*.example.com and http://*:29999. The user default has access_management and named_collection_control. For the sso suite, the server also gets http_authentication_servers.sso pointing to the token authenticator, and the web_console keys sso_name, sso_issuer, and sso_client_id.

Each suite can also run alone against another server, as described in utils/web-console/README.md; its checks then depend on that server's state, for example its component access policy.

Ports

All services listen on 127.0.0.1. The script checks the ports before it starts, and stops when one is in use.

PortService
38123HTTP of the server
39000Native protocol of the server
39181Embedded Keeper
39234Raft of the embedded Keeper
39099Nothing: the unavailable second shard of console_test
39900MinIO
39200Vault
39636OpenLDAP (LDAPS)
39080Keycloak
39700Token authenticator
32000-32999Endpoints of the lab clusters of the cluster agent

Logs

Everything of a run lives in tmp/console-e2e-run/ in the repository. The logs stay there after the run; the rest is removed. In tmp/console-e2e-run/logs/:

FileContents
<suite>.logOutput of a suite.
screenshots-<suite>/Screenshots of a suite.
bundle_module.logOutput of server_bundle_test.mjs.
clickhouse-server.log, clickhouse-server.err.logLogs of the server.
cluster-agent.logLog of the cluster agent.
sso-authenticator.logLog of the token authenticator.

Troubleshooting

MessageCause and fix
no clickhouse binary at <path>Build the binary, or pass --binary.
node is not installedInstall Node.js.
no Playwright in <dir>Create the workspace (see Prerequisites), or pass --e2e-dir.
Docker is not running, or this user cannot use itNeeded for backup, cluster, ldap, and sso.
the image <image> is not on this hostPull the image named in the message.
port <port> is in use: is another run still going?Stop the other run, or what --keep left.
the server did not startRead tmp/console-e2e-run/logs/clickhouse-server.err.log.
cannot create the bucket ch-backups in MinIOMinIO did not start: check docker logs console-e2e-minio.
Chromium reports missing librariesRun sudo npx playwright install-deps chromium in the workspace, or set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to a directory with the libraries before running the script.

reference/configuration.title: Web console configuration reference
reference/configuration.description: Every server configuration key that the web console reads or relies on: the web_console section, the console handler of http_handlers, HTTP authentication servers, and related settings.
reference/configuration.html:
The web console is configured in the ClickHouse server configuration, in files under config.d/. This page lists the web_console section, the console handler type of http_handlers with the default response headers, and the other server settings the console and its helper processes depend on. For the procedures, see Configure LDAP and Configure Keycloak single sign-on.

The web_console section

The section is read by ConsoleWebUIRequestHandler (src/Server/WebUIRequestHandler.cpp) on every request to undefined. Every key is a string. A key that is not set has its default; a key set to an empty value is empty, which turns off what the key controls. The values are public: the page reads them before anyone signs in, so no key may hold a secret.

KeyDefaultMeaning
source_code_urlhttps://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/Destination of Source code under Resources.
documentation_urlhttps://clickhouse.com/docs/Destination of Documentation under Resources, and the base of the links of the Console Guide to the rest of the ClickHouse documentation.
website_urlhttps://clickhouse.com/Destination of Website under Resources.
cloud_urlhttps://clickhouse.cloud/Destination of Cloud under Resources.
clickstack_url/clickstack/Address of ClickStack. A path on this server is embedded as a panel; an absolute URL of another origin is opened in a new tab, as a separate deployment with its own sign-in.
admin_databaseconsole_adminDatabase of the console tables. It must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$; otherwise the console reports that the setting is not a valid database name and the pages that need the tables are off.
backup_s3_endpointsEmptyS3-compatible endpoints allowed as backup destinations, separated by commas. See undefined. Empty: no S3 endpoint is allowed by the configuration.
sso_nameKeycloakName of the identity provider on the sign-in page: Sign in with followed by this name. See Single sign-on keys.
sso_issuerEmptyIssuer of the OpenID Connect provider. Empty: no single sign-on.
sso_client_idEmptyPublic client of the console at the provider. Empty: no single sign-on.
sso_scopesopenid profile emailScopes the console requests.
sso_username_claimpreferred_usernameClaim of the ID token that is the ClickHouse user name.

Destinations

source_code_url, documentation_url, website_url, cloud_url, and clickstack_url accept:

ValueEffect
A path on this server that starts with /, not with //, and contains no backslashOpened in the console (for clickstack_url, embedded as a panel).
An absolute http:// or https:// URLOpened in a new tab, with noopener and noreferrer.
EmptyThe destination is marked not configured.
Anything else, such as javascript: or //hostRejected: the destination is shown as not configured, with the reason that the address is not a valid HTTP(S) URL or server path.

For example, in a network without Internet access, point the documentation to an internal mirror and remove the other external links:

xml
<clickhouse>
    <web_console>
        <documentation_url>https://docs.example.internal/clickhouse/</documentation_url>
        <source_code_url></source_code_url>
        <website_url></website_url>
        <cloud_url></cloud_url>
    </web_console>
</clickhouse>

backup_s3_endpoints

The server does not check the endpoint of BACKUP ... TO S3 against remote_url_allow_hosts, so this list, together with the endpoints allowed in the console (the backup_endpoints table), is what restricts the S3 destinations of Backup & Restore. Each entry is one of:

EntryAllows
https://minio.example.com:9000Exactly this endpoint.
https://*.example.comAny subdomain of example.com, on the default port. Add :port to allow another port.
https://* or http://*:9000Any host with this scheme (and port).
*Any HTTP or HTTPS endpoint.

Patterns never match internal addresses: localhost, loopback and private network addresses, link-local addresses including 169.254.169.254, and names ending in .internal or .local; allow such an endpoint exactly. Link-local and metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, metadata.google.internal, instance-data) and patterns for any host (https://*, *) can be allowed only here, not in the console. Invalid entries are ignored, and the destination form lists them.

xml
<clickhouse>
    <web_console>
        <backup_s3_endpoints>http://10.0.4.20:9000, https://*.amazonaws.com</backup_s3_endpoints>
    </web_console>
</clickhouse>

For the destinations themselves, see Backup & Restore.

Single sign-on keys

The sign-in page offers Sign in with sso_name when both sso_issuer and sso_client_id are not empty. The values are public: the client of the console is a public client without a secret, and the server checks the access tokens through an HTTP authentication server (see undefined).

KeyDefaultMeaningWhen empty
sso_nameKeycloakLabel of the button and of the messages of the sign-in page.The console uses single sign-on.
sso_issuerEmptyIssuer URL of the provider, for example https://keycloak.example.com/realms/clickhouse. The console reads <sso_issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration. HTTPS; plain HTTP only for localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1]. A trailing / is removed.Single sign-on is off.
sso_client_idEmptyClient ID of the console at the provider. The provider must register the redirect URI <console origin>/console/oidc-callback and the post-logout redirect URI <console origin>/console/login for it.Single sign-on is off.
sso_scopesopenid profile emailThe scope of the authorization request.The console uses openid profile email.
sso_username_claimpreferred_usernameClaim of the verified ID token used as the ClickHouse user name. The token authenticator must use the same claim (SSO_USERNAME_CLAIM).The console uses preferred_username.
xml
<clickhouse>
    <web_console>
        <sso_name>Keycloak</sso_name>
        <sso_issuer>https://keycloak.example.com/realms/clickhouse</sso_issuer>
        <sso_client_id>clickhouse-console</sso_client_id>
    </web_console>
</clickhouse>

The deployment examples set these keys from the environment of the server container (utils/web-console/deploy/config.d/sso.xml):

xml
<clickhouse>
    <web_console>
        <sso_name from_env="SSO_NAME"/>
        <sso_issuer from_env="SSO_ISSUER"/>
        <sso_client_id from_env="SSO_CLIENT_ID"/>
    </web_console>
</clickhouse>

The console handler of http_handlers

The server serves the console by default for GET and HEAD requests to /console, and to any URI that starts with /console/, /console?, or /console#. To change its response headers, add a rule with the handler type console to undefined. The handler answers /console/config.json and /console/guide.json with their JSON documents and every other path with the page, so the rule must match every path under /console:

xml
<clickhouse>
    <http_handlers>
        <rule>
            <url>regex:^/console(/.*)?$</url>
            <methods>GET,HEAD</methods>
            <handler>
                <type>console</type>
                <http_response_headers>
                    <X-Frame-Options>SAMEORIGIN</X-Frame-Options>
                </http_response_headers>
            </handler>
        </rule>
        <defaults/>
    </http_handlers>
</clickhouse>

Keep <defaults/>, so that the other web UIs and the HTTP interface stay available.

Element of handlerMeaning
typeconsole.
http_response_headersHeaders to set, one element per header. A header set here replaces the default of the same name below.
content_typeContent-Type of the page. Default text/html; charset=UTF-8. /console/config.json and /console/guide.json are always application/json; charset=UTF-8.

Headers in http_handlers.common_http_response_headers apply to the console handler as to the other handlers.

Default response headers

The page, /console/config.json, and /console/guide.json are sent with these headers, unless the handler configuration sets a header of the same name:

HeaderValue
Cache-Controlno-store
X-Content-Type-Optionsnosniff
X-Frame-OptionsDENY
Referrer-Policyno-referrer
Content-Security-PolicySee below.

The Content-Security-Policy is:

text
default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; connect-src 'self' http: https:; frame-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'
DirectiveEffect
default-src 'none'Nothing is loaded unless another directive allows it.
script-src 'unsafe-inline', style-src 'unsafe-inline'Only the inline script and styles of the page run; no external script or stylesheet.
img-src data:Only images embedded as data: URLs.
connect-src 'self' http: https:Requests to this server, to other ClickHouse servers, and to the identity provider.
frame-src 'self'Only frames of the same origin: the embedded panels.
frame-ancestors 'none'No page may frame the console.
base-uri 'none', form-action 'none'No <base> element and no form submission.

These headers apply to the console only. The embedded pages (/dashboard, /merges, and the others) are served by their own handlers; do not set X-Frame-Options: DENY or frame-ancestors 'none' on them, or the console cannot embed them.

Related server configuration

http_authentication_servers

Single sign-on needs an HTTP authentication server that points to the token authenticator. The users that sign in with single sign-on are created IDENTIFIED WITH http SERVER '<name>' SCHEME 'BASIC', where <name> is the element name under http_authentication_servers (sso in the examples, and the default SSO_SERVER_NAME of the authenticator). See also HTTP authentication.

The keys of one server, as parsed by parseHTTPAuthParams (src/Access/ExternalAuthenticators.cpp):

KeyTypeDefaultMeaning
uriStringRequiredURL the server sends the GET request to, for example http://127.0.0.1:29700/. Its path and query are the path of the request.
connection_timeout_msInteger1000Connection timeout, in milliseconds.
receive_timeout_msInteger1000Receive timeout, in milliseconds.
send_timeout_msInteger1000Send timeout, in milliseconds.
max_triesInteger3Attempts per sign-in. Only a network error (an exception while sending or receiving) is retried; an answer such as 401 is final.
retry_initial_backoff_msInteger50Wait before the second attempt, in milliseconds. The wait doubles after each attempt.
retry_max_backoff_msInteger1000Longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
forward_headersList of elementsNoneNames of request headers of the client to forward to the authentication server, one element per header, for example <forward_headers><name>X-Request-Id</name></forward_headers>. Names are compared without case. A forwarded value that contains CR, LF, or NUL makes the sign-in fail with BAD_ARGUMENTS.

The configuration used by the deployment examples (utils/web-console/deploy/config.d/sso.xml):

xml
<clickhouse>
    <http_authentication_servers>
        <sso>
            <uri>http://sso-authenticator:29700/</uri>
            <connection_timeout_ms>1000</connection_timeout_ms>
            <receive_timeout_ms>2000</receive_timeout_ms>
            <send_timeout_ms>1000</send_timeout_ms>
            <max_tries>2</max_tries>
        </sso>
    </http_authentication_servers>
</clickhouse>

The HTTP contract between the server and the authenticator is in the token authenticator API.

user_directories.ldap

Directory sign-in uses an LDAP server in ldap_servers and an ldap user directory in user_directories. The Identity Providers → LDAP page generates this configuration, but does not install or change it. For the keys, see LDAP; for the procedure, see Configure LDAP.

backups.allowed_disk

A disk destination of Backup & Restore must be a disk of the server that is listed in backups.allowed_disk:

xml
<clickhouse>
    <storage_configuration>
        <disks>
            <backups>
                <type>local</type>
                <path>/var/lib/clickhouse/backups/</path>
            </backups>
        </disks>
    </storage_configuration>
    <backups>
        <allowed_disk>backups</allowed_disk>
    </backups>
</clickhouse>

See Backup and restore.

enable_webterminal

enable_webterminal (Bool, default true) enables the Web Terminal at /webterminal. When it is false, /webterminal answers 403 Forbidden, and the console shows the Web Terminal as unavailable with the reason that it is disabled on this server by the enable_webterminal server setting. The former name allow_experimental_webterminal is honored when enable_webterminal is not set.

Reload behavior

ChangeTakes effect
The web_console sectionAfter a configuration reload (SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG, or the automatic reload): the server reads the section on every request to /console/config.json. The page reads /console/config.json once when it loads, so open pages apply the change when they are loaded again.
http_authentication_serversAfter a configuration reload: the server parses the HTTP authentication servers again with the external authenticators.
A new ldap user directoryAfter a restart of the server: user directories are created when the server starts. Later changes of the LDAP server settings take effect with SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG.
A change of programs/server/console.html or another embedded pageAfter a rebuild of the clickhouse binary: the pages are embedded into it with #embed.

Remove the web_console section before downgrading to a server that does not know it: older servers reject unknown sections.

reference/http-endpoints.title: Web console HTTP endpoints and embedding contract
reference/http-endpoints.description: The HTTP paths of the web console, its routes and component IDs, /console/config.json, the OpenID Connect callback, the embedding contract of the panels, and the requests the console sends.

headings.text: Objects and tabs of the administration pages

reference/http-endpoints.html:
The console is one HTML page, programs/server/console.html, embedded into the clickhouse binary and served by ConsoleWebUIRequestHandler. Everything under /console returns that page, except /console/config.json and /console/guide.json; the page reads its route from the address and renders it in the browser. This page lists the paths, the routes, the component IDs, and the contract between the console and the pages it embeds. For the response headers and the console handler, see Configuration.

Server paths

PathMethodsResponse
/console, /console/..., /console?..., /console#...GET, HEADThe console page, text/html; charset=UTF-8, 200. Unknown paths under /console also return the page, which shows Page not found.
/console/config.jsonGET, HEADThe web_console configuration as JSON, application/json; charset=UTF-8, 200. See undefined.
/console/guide.jsonGET, HEADThe Console Guide, application/json; charset=UTF-8, 200. See undefined.
/console/oidc-callbackGET, HEADThe console page. In the browser it runs only the callback of a sign-in window. See undefined.

No path needs credentials: the page, the configuration, and the guide are public. Every query the page runs is authorized by the server with the credentials of the signed-in user.

Routes

The page parses location.pathname after /console (parseRoute), without leading and trailing /:

RouteMeaning
/consoleOpens /console/home when signed in, otherwise the sign-in page.
/console/loginThe sign-in page.
/console/login?next=<component id>The sign-in page; after sign-in, the console opens that component. next is accepted only when it is an ID of the component registry other than home, so it can never point outside the console. Signing in shows Sign in to open followed by the title of the component.
/console/<component id>The component, for example /console/merges or /console/admin-users.
/console/<component id>?tab=<tab>The component with one of its tabs.
/console/<administration page id>/<name>One object of an administration page: one more path segment, URL-encoded, without /.
/console/<administration page id>/<name>?tab=<tab>The same, on one of its tabs, for example /console/admin-users/alice?tab=roles.
/console/oidc-callbackThe redirect URI of OpenID Connect sign-ins.
Anything elsePage not found.

When nobody is signed in, every route except /console/login is replaced in the history by /console/login?next=<component id> (for a component route) or /console/login. After sign-in, the console replaces the address with /console/home or the next component. Navigation between components adds history entries, so the browser's Back and Forward buttons move between them.

Objects and tabs of the administration pages

Component IDObject segmenttab values (the first is the default)
admin-usersA user nameoverview, roles, privileges, limits, components, audit
admin-rolesA role nameprivileges, roles, members, limits, components
admin-data-accessNonecolumns, rows, effective, tests, attributes, rules, deployments
admin-accessNoneall (the default), role:<name>, or user:<name>: the subject of the policy editor
admin-limitsNoneprofiles, quotas
admin-auditNoneconsole, server, decisions. The parameter q fills in the search, for example ?tab=console&q=dap_. The default is console when the user can read the audit log, otherwise server.
admin-backupsNoneoverview, backups, server, restore, schedules, destinations, operations, verification
admin-clustersNoneinventory, create, register
admin-clustersA cluster ID (cluster_id)overview, nodes, keeper, configuration, scaling, maintenance, protection, operations, retirement

An unknown tab value opens the default tab.

Component IDs

The COMPONENTS registry describes every destination; the home page cards and the sidebar are generated from it.

IDCategoryTitleKindPath or configuration keyHow it receives the connection
homeHomeHomehome/console/home—
sqlWorkspaceSQL Consolepanel/ui/Form filling
dashboardWorkspaceDashboardpanel/dashboardEmbedding contract
clickstackWorkspaceClickStackpanelclickstack_urlNone: its own connection settings
terminalWorkspaceWeb Terminalpanel/webterminalWeb Terminal messages
binaryDiagnosticsBinary visualizerpanel/binaryEmbedding contract
mergesDiagnosticsMerges visualizerpanel/mergesEmbedding contract
schemaDiagnosticsSchema visualizerpanel/schemaEmbedding contract
jemallocDiagnosticsJemallocpanel/jemallocEmbedding contract
processors-profileDiagnosticsProcessors profilepanel/processors-profileEmbedding contract
admin-usersAdministrationUsersadmin/console/admin-users—
admin-rolesAdministrationRoles & Permissionsadmin/console/admin-roles—
admin-data-accessAdministrationData Access Policiesadmin/console/admin-data-access—
admin-accessAdministrationComponent Accessadmin/console/admin-access—
admin-limitsAdministrationProfiles & Quotasadmin/console/admin-limits—
admin-auditAdministrationAudit Activityadmin/console/admin-audit—
admin-clustersAdministrationClustersadmin/console/admin-clusters—
admin-backupsAdministrationBackup & Restoreadmin/console/admin-backups—
idp-ldapIdentity ProvidersLDAPadmin/console/idp-ldap—
idp-ssoIdentity ProvidersSSO (Keycloak)admin/console/idp-sso—
guideResourcesConsole Guideguide/console/guide (home page with the cards), /console/guide/<page>—
sourceResourcesSource codelinksource_code_urlNone: opened in a new tab
documentationResourcesDocumentationlinkdocumentation_urlNone: opened in a new tab

websiteResourcesWebsitelinkwebsite_urlNone: opened in a new tab
cloudResourcesCloudlinkcloud_urlNone: opened in a new tab
KindMeaning
homeThe home page of the console.
panelA page of this server embedded in a same-origin frame of the main area.
linkAn external destination, opened in a new tab with noopener and noreferrer.
adminA page rendered by the console itself.
guideThe Console Guide, rendered by the console from /console/guide.json. Like home, it is available to every signed-in user and is not governed by the console access policy.

The panels sql, dashboard, clickstack, terminal, and reference stay loaded (hidden) when another component is selected; the other panels are unloaded and loaded again when they are opened. The Binary visualizer loads Leaflet from cdnjs.cloudflare.com, and Jemalloc loads uPlot from cdn.jsdelivr.net: the console marks them as needing Internet access.

Which components a user sees, and the queries the console runs to decide it, are in Privileges.

/console/guide.json

The Console Guide is the documentation of the console, the pages under docs/products/web-console of the repository, shown inside the console. utils/web-console/build_guide.mjs converts them to HTML when they change and writes programs/server/console_guide.json, which is embedded into the clickhouse binary next to the page. So the guide needs no network access and matches the build of the server.

The page fetches /console/guide.json when the guide is first opened. The document has the title of the guide, the groups of pages of the navigation (groups, each with a title and the keys of its pages), and the pages by key, such as how-to/configure-ldap: the title, sidebar_title, and description of each page, its headings (id, level, text), and its content as HTML (html). The route of a page is /console/guide/<key>, and a heading is /console/guide/<key>#<id>. Links to other pages of the ClickHouse documentation keep their path in data-docs, and the page resolves them against documentation_url; without it, they are shown as text.

/console/config.json

The page fetches /console/config.json once when it loads, without credentials (credentials: 'omit', cache: 'no-store'). The response is one JSON object with every key of the web_console section, as strings, in this order, with the configured value or the default. With no web_console section, the response is:

json
{
  "source_code_url": "https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/",
  "documentation_url": "https://clickhouse.com/docs/",
  "website_url": "https://clickhouse.com/",
  "cloud_url": "https://clickhouse.cloud/",
  "clickstack_url": "/clickstack/",
  "admin_database": "console_admin",
  "backup_s3_endpoints": "",
  "sso_name": "Keycloak",
  "sso_issuer": "",
  "sso_client_id": "",
  "sso_scopes": "openid profile email",
  "sso_username_claim": "preferred_username"
}

The server writes it without spaces or line breaks. A key set to an empty value is returned as "". If the request fails, the page keeps its built-in defaults for the destination keys and admin_database. The meaning of each key is in Configuration.

/console/oidc-callback

/console/oidc-callback is the redirect URI of the sign-in window of an OpenID Connect provider: register <console origin>/console/oidc-callback as a valid redirect URI of the console's client. It is used by Sign in with on the sign-in page and by the test sign-in on Identity Providers → SSO (Keycloak).

When the provider redirects the window there, the page does not start the console. It:

  1. reads the parameters code, state, error, error_description, and iss from the query string, keeping only those present;
  2. replaces the address with /console/oidc-callback, without the query string;
  3. if state is present, posts the object of those parameters on the BroadcastChannel named console-oidc, and closes the channel;
  4. shows The sign-in has finished: you can close this window., and closes the window after 300 milliseconds. Without state, it shows This page receives the answer of an identity provider. Open the console instead.

The message on console-oidc:

FieldTypeMeaning
codeStringThe authorization code, when the provider accepted the sign-in.
stateStringThe state of the authorization request. The console page that opened the window accepts only a message with the state it generated.
errorStringThe OAuth error, when the provider refused the sign-in.
error_descriptionStringThe description of the error, when the provider gave one.
issStringThe issuer that sent the answer (RFC 9207), when the provider sends it. The console refuses an answer whose iss is not the issuer of the discovery document.

The message carries no token and no PKCE verifier: the verifier stays in the memory of the console page that opened the window, and the code cannot be exchanged for tokens without it. The opening page waits at most 5 minutes for the message; if the window is closed earlier, it reports that the sign-in window was closed before the sign-in finished.

Embedding contract

The console embeds the pages of the server in same-origin frames and hands them the connection without a URL, browser storage, or a message to another origin. Each kind of page has its own mechanism.

Native pages

The pages /dashboard, /binary, /merges, /schema, /jemalloc, /processors-profile, and /docs (programs/server/{dashboard,binary,merges,schema,jemalloc,processors_profile,docs}.html) call, once and synchronously at startup:

javascript
window.parent.clickhouseConsole.getConnection(window)

window.clickhouseConsole is a frozen, non-writable object of the console page:

MemberValue
version1
getConnection(panel_window)The connection, or null.

getConnection returns a frozen object only when someone is signed in, and panel_window is the window of a frame that the console created for a panel of this kind in the current session. Otherwise it returns null.

Field of the resultMeaning
urlURL of the ClickHouse server the console is connected to.
userUser name of the session.
passwordPassword of the session, or the current access token after single sign-on.

A page that is not embedded (window.parent === window), or whose parent is of another origin (reading window.parent.clickhouseConsole throws), does not use the contract and behaves as when it is opened on its own. When it receives a connection, the page uses it instead of the one from its own address, and hides its connection fields.

Credential updates

After single sign-on, the console refreshes the access token before it expires: at 70% of its lifetime (expires_in, 300 seconds when the provider does not report it), and at the earliest after 10 seconds. It then posts the new credentials to the frame of every native page of the session, with its own origin as the target origin:

javascript
{type: 'console-credentials', user: '<user name>', password: '<new access token>'}

Each native page accepts the message only when it received a connection from getConnection, the message comes from window.parent and from its own origin, and user is the user of its connection. It then replaces the password it uses. The SQL Console, the Web Terminal, and ClickStack do not receive these messages: they keep the token they started with until they are reloaded.

Web Terminal messages

/webterminal (programs/server/webterminal.html) uses postMessage. The console sends its messages to the terminal frame only, with its own origin as the target origin, and accepts messages only from that frame and from its own origin.

MessageDirectionWhenEffect
{type: 'webterminal-hello'}Console to terminalWhen the frame has loadedThe terminal remembers the origin of its parent, so that it can post back to it.
{type: 'webterminal-credentials', user, password}Console to terminalRight after webterminal-helloThe terminal connects with these credentials, if it is waiting for them. Embedded without a user in its URL, the terminal waits for this message and shows Waiting for credentials... (press Enter to log in manually).
{type: 'webterminal-refit', focus: false}Console to terminalWhen the terminal panel is shown againThe terminal fits its size to the frame, without taking the focus.
{type: 'webterminal-escape'}Terminal to consoleThe user presses Escape in the terminalThe console moves the focus to the sidebar entry of the terminal, or to the Console button when its navigation is hidden.
{type: 'webterminal-closed'}Terminal to consoleThe clickhouse-client session ended after it was openThe console removes the frame and shows The terminal session ended with Reload panel.

The terminal accepts messages only from window.parent, and only from the same origin, *.clickhouse.com, or *.clickhouse.cloud over HTTPS.

SQL Console

The SQL Console (/ui/) has no embedding interface. When its frame has loaded, the console:

  1. waits up to 20 seconds for the connection form or the connected layout of the SQL Console;
  2. if it is already connected, does nothing more;
  3. otherwise fills in the URL, user, and password fields of the form, and selects its connect button, as a user would;
  4. waits up to 30 seconds for the connected layout, or for the button to become enabled again after it was disabled, which means the connection failed.

On failure, the console clears the password field of the form, and shows a notice above the panel: Automatic sign-in to the SQL Console did not succeed: followed by the reason (the form did not appear, it has an unexpected layout, it did not finish connecting within 30 seconds, or the error it reported). The user can then sign in with the form of the SQL Console.

ClickStack

ClickStack has its own connection settings, entered in ClickStack on first use; the console does not sign in to it. Before it loads ClickStack, the console stores "closed" under the local storage key clickstack-banner-state of the origin, which closes the banner of ClickStack, and shows the banner's message in a popup the first time ClickStack is opened after each sign-in, unless Do not show this again was selected (local storage key console.clickstack-notice).

Navigation away from a panel

When the page inside a panel frame navigates to a path outside the panel's own path, for example the Logout of the SQL Console, which goes to /, the console removes the frame and offers Reload panel.

Requests the console sends

Queries

Every query is a POST to the root of the ClickHouse HTTP interface of the connection (<server URL>/), with the SQL text as the body:

PartValue
Content-Typetext/plain; charset=UTF-8
X-ClickHouse-UserThe user of the session.
X-ClickHouse-KeyThe password of the session, or the access token after single sign-on.
URL parametersparam_<name> for the query parameters, bound by the server ({name:Type}); settings by their names; add_http_cors_header=1 when the server is of another origin than the page. No credential is ever in the URL.
Fetch optionscredentials: 'omit', cache: 'no-store', referrerPolicy: 'no-referrer'

The console checks credentials at sign-in with SELECT currentUser() AS user, version() AS version, hostName() AS hostname FORMAT JSON, which needs no privilege. It tells errors apart by the X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code header (or Code: in the body):

CodesReported as
192, 193, 194, 516, or HTTP 401 without a codeThe username or password is incorrect.
195This user is not allowed to connect from your network address.
497, 164, 446, or HTTP 403 without a codeThe user does not have the required permissions.
60, 81, 46A required system table or function is not available on this server.
OtherThe server returned an error.

Route probes

After sign-in, the console sends HEAD requests without credentials to the routes of optional panels: /webterminal answers 403 when enable_webterminal is off, and the ClickStack path answers 404 when the build has no ClickStack bundle. For the diagnostic panels, it runs their probe queries with LIMIT 0 (see Privileges).

Identity provider requests

With single sign-on, the browser also sends, without credentials of ClickHouse:

RequestToPurpose
GET <sso_issuer>/.well-known/openid-configurationThe providerDiscovery.
Navigation of the sign-in window to the authorization_endpointThe providerresponse_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri (<origin>/console/oidc-callback), scope (sso_scopes), state, nonce, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256.
POST to the token_endpoint, grant_type=authorization_codeThe providerExchanges the code, with code_verifier.
GET of the jwks_uriThe providerKeys to verify the ID token and the access token.
POST to the token_endpoint, grant_type=refresh_tokenThe providerRefreshes the access token. When the provider refuses, the console signs out and shows that the session has ended.
Navigation to the end_session_endpointThe providerOn sign-out: client_id, id_token_hint, and post_logout_redirect_uri (<origin>/console/login).

The provider must allow the origin of the console as a web origin of the client, or the browser blocks the token request. The server then checks the access token through the token authenticator.

reference/console-tables.title: Web console tables
reference/console-tables.description: Every table the web console creates in its admin database, with every column, type, and meaning, the versioning model, the reader role, and which process writes each table.
reference/console-tables.html:
The console keeps its own state in ordinary tables of one database, named by the admin_database setting (default console_admin; see Configuration). The tables are created only when an administrator selects Set up on a page, with CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS and CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so running a setup again is safe. The DDL below is the one in programs/server/console.html (ADMIN_TABLES, DAP_TABLES, BACKUP_TABLES, CLUSTER_TABLES, IDP_TABLES).

The tables are stored on the server the console is connected to and are not replicated. To remove the console's data, drop the database; the console then works as if it was never set up.

Versioning model

The tables follow two patterns:

PatternEngineHow a change is writtenHow it is read
Current stateReplacingMergeTree(updated_at) with the key of the object in ORDER BYA new row with the whole object replaces the previous version. Removing the object inserts a row with deleted = true.FINAL ... WHERE NOT deleted
HistoryMergeTreeRows are appended and never updated.The latest row, or all of them

The writer and the time of each row are columns the server fills in:

  • updated_by, created_by, requested_by, recorded_by, ran_by, and actor are MATERIALIZED currentUser();
  • updated_at, created_at, requested_at, at, ran_at, and event_time are MATERIALIZED now64(3);
  • server_host of audit_log is MATERIALIZED hostName().

Each such writer column has a CHECK constraint (for example CONSTRAINT updated_by_is_writer CHECK updated_by = currentUser()) that rejects any other value, also when insert_allow_materialized_columns is enabled. A user who can insert into a table therefore cannot write rows in another user's name. The tables are ordinary tables, though: users with ALTER, TRUNCATE, or DROP on them can change or remove rows, so they are not tamper-proof. Grant SELECT and INSERT only, and keep ALTER and DROP to the server administrators.

All times are DateTime64(3, 'UTC') unless noted. Columns that hold JSON are String.

Reader role

The Set up of Component Access also creates the role <admin_database>_reader (by default console_admin_reader) with SELECT on component_policy, and offers to grant it to the users and roles created with SQL. Users who cannot read the policy do not see the components it governs, so every console user needs this role among their default roles (or SELECT on the table). A role is used because granting it needs only the admin option on the role, while granting SELECT on the table directly would need it WITH GRANT OPTION.

Administration tables

Created by Set up on Component Access, which also inserts one rule per governed component for all users (open true; view_data and run_queries true for panels; administer false), and a setup record in the audit log. The retention of the audit log is chosen in the dialog: 1 to 36500 days, default 365.

audit_log

sql
CREATE TABLE console_admin.audit_log
(
    event_time DateTime64(3, 'UTC') MATERIALIZED now64(3),
    actor String MATERIALIZED currentUser(),
    server_host LowCardinality(String) MATERIALIZED hostName(),
    correlation_id UUID,
    scope String,
    target_type LowCardinality(String),
    target_name String,
    action LowCardinality(String),
    summary String,
    result Enum8('success' = 1, 'failure' = 2, 'partial' = 3),
    error String,
    details String,
    CONSTRAINT actor_is_writer CHECK actor = currentUser(),
    CONSTRAINT host_is_server CHECK server_host = hostName()
)
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY event_time
TTL toDateTime(event_time) + INTERVAL 365 DAY
ColumnTypeMeaning
event_timeDateTime64(3, 'UTC')When the record was written. Filled in by the server.
actorStringThe user who wrote the record. Filled in by the server.
server_hostLowCardinality(String)Host name of the server that stored the record. Filled in by the server.
correlation_idUUIDID of the change. The console also sets it as the log_comment of the statements of the change; for backup and cluster operations, it is the operation ID.
scopeStringlocal, or cluster:<name> for a change applied ON CLUSTER.
target_typeLowCardinality(String)Kind of object changed, for example user, role, platform, backup, or data_access.
target_nameStringName of the object changed.
actionLowCardinality(String)What was done, for example setup, delete_role, dap_reconcile, server_bundle, recovery_rehearsal, or sso_create_user.
summaryStringOne-line description.
resultEnum8success, failure, or partial (a change that took effect on some servers or steps only).
errorStringSanitized error message: passwords and keys are masked.
detailsStringJSON with the steps and their outcome on each server, and other details of the action.

To change the retention later: ALTER TABLE console_admin.audit_log MODIFY TTL toDateTime(event_time) + INTERVAL <days> DAY.

component_policy

sql
CREATE TABLE console_admin.component_policy
(
    subject_type Enum8('all' = 1, 'role' = 2, 'user' = 3),
    subject String,
    component LowCardinality(String),
    open Bool,
    view_data Bool,
    run_queries Bool,
    administer Bool,
    deleted Bool DEFAULT false,
    updated_at DateTime64(3, 'UTC') MATERIALIZED now64(3),
    updated_by String MATERIALIZED currentUser(),
    CONSTRAINT updated_by_is_writer CHECK updated_by = currentUser()
)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at) ORDER BY (subject_type, subject, component)
ColumnTypeMeaning
subject_typeEnum8all (every user), role, or user.
subjectStringRole or user name; empty for all.
componentLowCardinality(String)A component ID.
openBoolThe subject may open the component. The only capability the console enforces.
view_dataBoolCapability View data: compared with the native privileges that govern it.
run_queriesBoolCapability Run queries.
administerBoolCapability Administer.
deletedBoolThe rule is removed.
updated_at, updated_byTime and writer of the version.

A capability is allowed when any rule for all users, for the signed-in user, or for one of the roles enabled in the session allows it. A component without any row is not governed and stays open to everyone.

protected_accounts

sql
CREATE TABLE console_admin.protected_accounts
(
    name String,
    reason String,
    deleted Bool DEFAULT false,
    updated_at DateTime64(3, 'UTC') MATERIALIZED now64(3),
    updated_by String MATERIALIZED currentUser(),
    CONSTRAINT updated_by_is_writer CHECK updated_by = currentUser()
)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at) ORDER BY name
ColumnTypeMeaning
nameStringUser name that the console does not delete or suspend.

Server bundle tables

The backup worker stores each server bundle in a temporary table server_bundle_<id>, where <id> is the first 16 hexadecimal characters of the operation ID, with the columns part UInt32, kind Enum8('header' = 1, 'data' = 2, 'tag' = 3), and data String. It backs the table up with BACKUP TABLE, and drops it. A bundle restore brings it back as server_bundle_restore_<id> and drops it after use. The tables hold only ciphertext.

reference/privileges.title: Web console privileges
reference/privileges.description: The privileges each panel and page of the web console needs to be listed and to act, the capability checks the console runs, the cluster capabilities, and the service accounts of the helper processes.
reference/privileges.html:
Every query and statement of the console runs with the credentials of the signed-in user and is authorized by the ClickHouse server. The console asks the server what the user can do only to decide what to list and which buttons to offer: a wrong or stale answer shows or hides a button, it does not grant anything. See Security model and GRANT.

A component is listed when both hold:

  1. the server allows what the component reads: the probe queries of a panel, or one of the capability checks of an administration page;
  2. the component access policy allows Open for the user or one of the roles enabled in the session, or no rule mentions the component yet. Home and Component Access are not governed by the policy.

Panels

After sign-in, the console runs the probe queries of each panel once, joined with UNION ALL. When the server refuses them, the panel is not listed; when a system table does not exist, it is shown as unavailable. The capability columns show the native privileges the Component Access page compares with the policy (COMPONENT_NATIVE).

ComponentProbe queriesView dataRun queriesAdminister
sql SQL ConsoleNoneSame as Run queriesEvery query is authorized by the grants on the tables it uses.—
dashboard DashboardSELECT 1 FROM system.dashboards LIMIT 0SELECT on system.dashboards, system.metric_log, system.asynchronous_metric_logCharts can be edited to run any query the user is allowed to run.—
clickstack ClickStackNone (a HEAD request to its path)Its own connection settings and authorization——
terminal Web TerminalNone (a HEAD request to /webterminal)—Every query is authorized by the grants of the user. Enabled for everyone by enable_webterminal.—
binary Binary visualizerSELECT addressToSymbol(toUInt64(0)) LIMIT 0 SETTINGS allow_introspection_functions = 1INTROSPECTION——
merges Merges visualizerSELECT 1 FROM system.part_log LIMIT 0SELECT on system.part_log——
schema Schema visualizerSELECT 1 FROM system.tables LIMIT 0, SELECT 1 FROM system.columns LIMIT 0SELECT on system.tables, system.columns, system.dictionaries——
jemalloc JemallocSELECT 1 FROM system.jemalloc_stats LIMIT 0SELECT on system.jemalloc_stats, system.asynchronous_metrics—SYSTEM JEMALLOC
processors-profile Processors profileSELECT 1 FROM system.processors_profile_log LIMIT 0, SELECT 1 FROM system.query_log LIMIT 0SELECT on system.processors_profile_log, system.query_log——
reference ReferenceSELECT 1 FROM system.documentation LIMIT 0SELECT on system.documentation——

Links of Resources need no privilege; the policy only lists or hides them.

Pages

An administration page is listed when at least one of its checks passes, and the policy allows Open. What the user can do on it is decided by native privileges (ADMIN_NATIVE); the console offers each action only when the matching check passes.

PageListed when any of these checks passesTo readTo act

Capability checks

A grant check runs CHECK GRANT <privilege> and passes when the server answers 1. <db> is the admin database; the checks on its tables are skipped when admin_database is not a valid name.

CHECK GRANT ... ON *.* does not report user and role management granted for name patterns (GRANT ALTER USER ON app_* TO ...). The console reads those patterns from the user's own SHOW GRANTS FINAL and offers the actions for the matching names; per-user actions are checked with CHECK GRANT on the user.

Backup actions

ActionPrivileges
See the pageSELECT on backup_operations, backup_events, backup_destinations, backup_schedules
Back upBACKUP on the scope; READ, WRITE ON DISK, or NAMED COLLECTION on the destination's collection and READ, WRITE ON S3; INSERT on backup_operations, backup_events, and audit_log

Check an artifactCREATE DATABASE, DROP DATABASE ON console_inspect_*.* (the artifact is opened with the Backup database engine)
Manage destinationsINSERT on backup_destinations; for S3, CREATE NAMED COLLECTION, ALTER NAMED COLLECTION, DROP NAMED COLLECTION on console_backup_*
Allow S3 endpointsSELECT and INSERT on backup_endpoints
Manage schedulesINSERT on backup_schedules

READ ON S3 and WRITE ON S3 apply to every S3 URL, not only to the configured destinations, and READ ON DISK and WRITE ON DISK to every disk: grant them only to users trusted with that. The role templates that bundle these privileges are described in Backup & Restore.

Cluster capabilities

Each capability is a column of the cluster_capabilities table (engine Null), granted as INSERT(<column>), for example GRANT INSERT(scale) ON console_admin.cluster_capabilities TO cluster_operator. The console checks them with CHECK GRANT to offer actions; the cluster agent checks them again with EXECUTE AS <requester> CHECK GRANT before it executes an operation. Requesting an operation also needs INSERT on cluster_operations, cluster_events, and cluster_revisions.

CapabilityLabel in the console

TemplateGrants
Cluster ViewerSELECT on the cluster tables and backup_destinations; view_clusters.

Service accounts

utils/web-console/deploy/service-accounts.sql creates the accounts of the helper processes with these privileges. Run it as an administrator after Set up on the pages that create the console tables, with the passwords as query parameters:

bash
clickhouse-client --user default --password ... --param_backup_pw=... --param_policy_pw=... --param_agent_pw=... --param_sso_pw=... \
    --multiquery < service-accounts.sql

Lines with a placeholder in angle brackets are commented out: replace the placeholder and remove the comment marker. The statements below use the default admin database console_admin. For the procedure, see Create service accounts.

Backup worker

sql
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS backup_worker IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY {backup_pw:String};
-- GRANT <role made with the Backup Administrator template> TO backup_worker;
GRANT CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, INSERT, SELECT, BACKUP ON console_admin.server_bundle* TO backup_worker;

The role is made with the Backup Administrator template on Roles & Permissions, for the databases of the schedules; the template lists its exact privileges before it creates the role. The worker also needs SELECT on those databases for fingerprints, and INSERT on the backup tables and audit_log. The grant on server_bundle* is needed only with BUNDLE_KEY_PROVIDER.

Access policy worker

sql
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS access_policy_worker IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY {policy_pw:String};
GRANT SELECT ON console_admin.* TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT INSERT ON console_admin.dap_owned TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT INSERT ON console_admin.dap_deployments TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT INSERT ON console_admin.audit_log TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT INSERT ON console_admin.dap_user_attributes TO access_policy_worker;      -- only with an attribute feed
GRANT SELECT ON system.users TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT SELECT ON system.roles TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT SELECT ON system.role_grants TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT SELECT ON system.grants TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT SELECT ON system.row_policies TO access_policy_worker;
GRANT SHOW USERS, SHOW ROLES, SHOW ROW POLICIES ON *.* TO access_policy_worker;
-- GRANT IMPERSONATE ON <each rule author> TO access_policy_worker;

The worker holds no privilege to grant anything: it runs each statement as EXECUTE AS <rule author>, so the server checks the author's own privileges, including the grant option and CLUSTER for ON CLUSTER. IMPERSONATE needs allow_impersonate_user on the server.

Token authenticator

Checking tokens needs no account. The user sync needs:

sql
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS sso_sync IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY {sso_pw:String};
GRANT CREATE USER, ALTER USER, DROP USER ON *.* TO sso_sync;
GRANT SHOW USERS, SHOW ROLES ON *.* TO sso_sync;
GRANT SELECT ON system.users TO sso_sync;
GRANT SELECT ON system.roles TO sso_sync;
GRANT SELECT ON system.role_grants TO sso_sync;
GRANT INSERT ON console_admin.audit_log TO sso_sync;
-- GRANT <role> TO sso_sync WITH ADMIN OPTION;

Grant each role the groups give WITH ADMIN OPTION, so that the sync can grant only those, or ROLE ADMIN for every role. Roles named in SSO_DEFAULT_ROLES also need the admin option.

Cluster agent

sql
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS cluster_agent IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY {agent_pw:String};
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON console_admin.clusters TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON console_admin.cluster_revisions TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON console_admin.cluster_operations TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON console_admin.cluster_events TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON console_admin.cluster_observations TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON console_admin.cluster_resources TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT ON console_admin.cluster_capabilities TO cluster_agent;
GRANT SELECT ON console_admin.backup_destinations TO cluster_agent;
GRANT INSERT ON console_admin.audit_log TO cluster_agent;
-- GRANT IMPERSONATE ON <each user who requests cluster operations> TO cluster_agent;

Recovery rehearsal

service-accounts.sql creates no account for the recovery rehearsal. The user given with --user needs SELECT on the console tables and INSERT on backup_events and audit_log.

reference/helper-processes.html:
The console runs in the browser and can only send queries to the server. What a browser cannot do, such as running schedules, deleting backups, creating containers, or checking single sign-on tokens, is done by helper processes in utils/web-console/. Each is one Node.js script without packages (Node.js 18 or later), configured with environment variables, and documented in its header comment. All but the recovery rehearsal are also in the tools image.

All of them except the token authenticator connect to the HTTP interface of the server with a service account (CLICKHOUSE_URL, CLICKHOUSE_USER, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD), send credentials in the X-ClickHouse-User and X-ClickHouse-Key headers, and keep their state in the console tables. The privileges of each account are in Privileges.

ProcessScriptTools image commandRuns
Backup workerbackup_worker.mjs (with server_bundle.mjs)backup-workerContinuously, next to the server
Cluster agentcluster_agent.mjscluster-agentContinuously, on the infrastructure host
Access policy workeraccess_policy_worker.mjsaccess-policy-workerContinuously
Token authenticatorsso_authenticator.mjssso-authenticatorContinuously, reachable only by the server
Recovery rehearsalrecovery_rehearsal.mjsNoneOn demand, on the server host

Backup worker

utils/web-console/backup_worker.mjs does what Backup & Restore cannot do in the browser. Each cycle it:

  • records a heartbeat (a check event named heartbeat for worker:<WORKER_ID> in backup_events), shown on the Overview;
  • reconciles unfinished operations, after a browser closed or the server restarted;
  • submits due scheduled backups (BACKUP ... ASYNC), and restore tests of schedules that ask for them;
  • makes second copies of scheduled full backups at the schedule's second destination;
  • applies retention, and checks the protection (encryption, Object Lock, versioning) of enabled S3 destinations every 6 hours;
  • executes requested deletions, tests listing and deleting at destinations, and removes destination test artifacts;
  • with BUNDLE_KEY_PROVIDER, makes and restores server bundles;
  • calls a schedule's webhook when a scheduled operation fails.

Several workers can run at the same time: a scheduled run has a deterministic operation ID and artifact path, and the server refuses a second backup with the same ID or location. For the model, see Backup & Restore.

Running the backup worker

bash
CLICKHOUSE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8123 CLICKHOUSE_USER=backup_worker CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=... \
PROD_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... PROD_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... \
node utils/web-console/backup_worker.mjs

With the tools image, the command is backup-worker. Run it on the server host, or with the server's data directory mounted: deleting from a disk destination needs the disk's directory.

Arguments of the backup worker

ArgumentMeaning
NoneRun cycles every INTERVAL_SECONDS until stopped.
--onceRun one cycle and exit.
bundle-key-init --key-file <path>Create a master key file for the file provider. --key-file defaults to BUNDLE_KEY_FILE.
bundle --destination <name>Make a server bundle now, to the enabled destination of that name. --destination defaults to BUNDLE_DESTINATION.
bundle-restore --bundle <operation ID> --mode compareCompare a server bundle with the files of this host.
bundle-restore --bundle <operation ID> --mode stageWrite the files of a server bundle into a new staging directory. --mode defaults to compare.

The bundle* commands are for a person on the worker host. They are the only way to make and restore bundles with the passphrase provider, which reads the passphrase from a terminal without echoing it.

Environment variables of the backup worker

VariableDefaultMeaning
CLICKHOUSE_URLhttp://127.0.0.1:8123HTTP interface of the server.
CLICKHOUSE_USERdefaultService account.
CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORDEmptyIts password.
ADMIN_DATABASEconsole_adminDatabase of the console tables. Must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.
WORKER_IDHost name and process IDName in the heartbeat and the logs.
INTERVAL_SECONDS30Time between cycles.
<REF>_ACCESS_KEY_ID, <REF>_SECRET_ACCESS_KEYNoneS3 credentials of the destinations whose credential reference is <REF>.
<REF>_REGIONus-east-1Region used to sign the S3 requests of those destinations.
<NOTIFY_REF>NoneWebhook URL of the schedules whose failure notification (notify_ref) is <NOTIFY_REF>.

Server bundles

BACKUP does not copy the server's configuration files, the secrets in them, TLS keys, scripts, or Keeper's own state. The worker backs those up as server bundles (server_bundle.mjs): it reads the files on its host, encrypts them as one stream, stores the ciphertext in a temporary table server_bundle_<id>, backs that table up to a destination with BACKUP TABLE, and drops it. The server and the destination only hold ciphertext. A restore brings the table back under another name (server_bundle_restore_<id>), checks and decrypts it, and either compares the files with this host or writes them to a staging directory; it never writes into the server's configuration.

Format version 1: a clear JSON header (the cipher, the key provider, and the wrapped data key; no file names, sizes, or checksums), the AES-256-GCM ciphertext of a gzip stream of records with the header as additional authenticated data, and the authentication tag. Each bundle has a new random 256-bit data key, wrapped by the key provider.

VariableDefaultMeaning
BUNDLE_KEY_PROVIDERUnset: no bundlesfile, vault, or passphrase.
BUNDLE_KEY_FILENonefile provider: the master key file, made with bundle-key-init. It must be readable by its owner only (mode 600); a file readable by others is refused. It is never included in a bundle.
VAULT_ADDRNonevault provider: address of HashiCorp Vault.
VAULT_TOKENNonevault provider: token that may encrypt and decrypt with the Transit key.
VAULT_TOKEN_FILENonevault provider: file with the token, read when VAULT_TOKEN is not set.
VAULT_TRANSIT_KEYNonevault provider: name of the Transit key.
VAULT_TRANSIT_MOUNTtransitvault provider: mount of the Transit secrets engine.
VAULT_NAMESPACEEmptyvault provider: Vault namespace.
BUNDLE_PATHS/etc/clickhouse-serverFiles and directories to include, separated by commas. A file the worker cannot read fails the bundle.
BUNDLE_KEEPEREmptyhost:port of Keeper: the worker asks it for a new snapshot (csnp) and includes it. Needs BUNDLE_KEEPER_SNAPSHOTS.
BUNDLE_KEEPER_SNAPSHOTSEmptySnapshot directory of Keeper.
BUNDLE_STAGING_DIR/var/lib/clickhouse-console/restore-stagingWhere stage restores write files.
BUNDLE_COMPARE_ROOT/Root under which the paths of a bundle are compared with this host.
BUNDLE_DESTINATIONEmptyDestination of automatic bundles (not with passphrase).
BUNDLE_EVERY_HOURS0Interval of automatic bundles, in hours; 0: only on request.
ProviderWhere the master key isBundles from the console and on a schedule
fileA file on the worker host, readable by its owner only. Keep a copy out of band: without it, no bundle can be decrypted.Yes
vaultThe Transit secrets engine of Vault; the key never leaves Vault.Yes
passphraseNowhere: derived from a passphrase with scrypt; at least 12 characters.No: only the bundle and bundle-restore commands

bundle-key-init refuses to replace an existing file, prints the fingerprint of the key (sha256: followed by 16 hexadecimal characters), and reminds you to copy the key out of band.

Files of the backup worker

FileAccessWhen
Directories of disk destinations, under the path of the disk in system.disksRead, deleteDeletions, retention, and destination tests of disk destinations. Only under <disk path>/<prefix>/<artifact>.
BUNDLE_PATHSReadMaking a bundle.
