Logs and exit codes of the backup worker

The worker writes one JSON object per line to standard output, without credentials: {"time": "<ISO time>", "worker": "<WORKER_ID>", "message": "...", ...}, for example the messages started and cycle failed. A failed cycle is logged and the next cycle runs after the interval. The bundle* commands print their result, and on failure print error: <message> to standard error and exit with code 1.

Cluster agent

utils/web-console/cluster_agent.mjs executes the lifecycle operations of Clusters on the infrastructure host. It:

  • executes queued operations with checkpoints, one at a time per cluster, after checking on the server that the requester holds the capability (EXECUTE AS <requester> CHECK GRANT);
  • provisions and changes clusters through a provider: docker-compose (a local lab, always available) and kubernetes (with the ClickHouse operator, when CLUSTER_AGENT_KUBECONFIG is set);
  • observes every registered cluster and records what it saw;
  • records a heartbeat each cycle (cluster_events, kind heartbeat, op_id agent:<AGENT_ID>) with its providers, environments, and public key.

It runs only docker and kubectl, with fixed argument lists, never through a shell. For the model, see Clusters.

Running the cluster agent

bash
CLICKHOUSE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8123 CLICKHOUSE_USER=cluster_agent CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=... \
CLUSTER_AGENT_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/clickhouse-console/clusters CLUSTER_AGENT_ENVIRONMENTS=lab,development \
node utils/web-console/cluster_agent.mjs

With the tools image, the command is cluster-agent. The docker-compose provider needs the docker CLI with Compose v2 and access to the Docker socket, which is equivalent to root on the host; utils/web-console/deploy/compose.cluster-agent.yaml runs the agent with the host network and the socket.

ArgumentMeaning
NoneRun cycles every INTERVAL_SECONDS until stopped.
--onceRun one cycle, observing every cluster, and exit.

Environment variables of the cluster agent

VariableDefaultMeaning
CLICKHOUSE_URLhttp://127.0.0.1:8123The server with the console tables.
CLICKHOUSE_USERdefaultService account.
CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORDEmptyIts password.

Files of the cluster agent

FileMeaning
CLUSTER_AGENT_STATE_DIR/agent-key.pemThe agent's RSA key pair (3072 bits), mode 600, created on first use. The console encrypts the administrator password of a new cluster with its public key. Back it up.
CLUSTER_AGENT_STATE_DIR/chc-<id>/One directory per docker-compose cluster: compose.yaml, the node configuration, secrets.env (mode 600, with CH_ADMIN_PASSWORD, CH_CLUSTER_SECRET, CH_INTERSERVER_PASSWORD, CH_PROXY_PASSWORD), .console-hashes.json, and .console-applied-settings.json.

The directory is created with mode 700. Docker objects carry the labels io.clickhouse.console.cluster and io.clickhouse.console.managed-by; the agent stops or deletes only objects with the labels of the cluster it works on.

Logs and exit codes of the cluster agent

One JSON object per line on standard output: {"time": "<ISO time>", "agent": "<AGENT_ID>", "message": "...", ...}, for example started, cycle failed, and observation failed. Without --once, a failed cycle is logged and the next one runs. With --once, a failed cycle exits with code 1.

Access policy worker

utils/web-console/access_policy_worker.mjs keeps the native access controls in line with the policy rules of Data Access Policies when nobody has the console open. Each cycle it:

  1. imports user attributes from a feed, when one is configured: only attributes defined with the feed's source, and values the feed no longer reports are removed;
  2. computes the desired state of every enabled rule with the same functions as the console, which it loads from console.html;
  3. applies the difference: it creates, changes, and removes only entities recorded in dap_owned, and never restores an owned entity that was removed outside the platform;
  4. records ownership in dap_owned, a reconcile deployment in dap_deployments, and a dap_reconcile audit record.

Each statement runs as EXECUTE AS <author>, the author of the current revision of the rule, so the server checks that user's privileges. For the model, see Data Access Policies.

Running the access policy worker

bash
CLICKHOUSE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8123 CLICKHOUSE_USER=access_policy_worker CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=... \
ATTRIBUTE_FEED=/var/lib/clickhouse-console/hr-feed.json ATTRIBUTE_FEED_SOURCE=hr INTERVAL_SECONDS=60 \
node utils/web-console/access_policy_worker.mjs

With the tools image, the command is access-policy-worker.

ArgumentMeaning
NoneRun cycles every INTERVAL_SECONDS until stopped.
--onceRun one cycle and exit.

VariableDefaultMeaning

CLICKHOUSE_USERdefaultService account.
CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORDEmptyIts password.

ATTRIBUTE_FEED_TOKENEmptyBearer token for an https:// feed.

LDAP attributes

The attributes can come from an LDAP directory instead of ATTRIBUTE_FEED. Setting both ATTRIBUTE_FEED and LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_URL is refused: one worker imports from one source.

VariableDefaultMeaning
LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_URLEmpty: no LDAP importldaps://host[:636], or ldap://host[:389] with LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_STARTTLS=1. Plain LDAP is refused.
LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_STARTTLSEmpty1: use StartTLS on an ldap:// URL.
LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_CA_FILEThe system's certificate authoritiesCertificate authority of the LDAP server. The certificate is always checked.
LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_BIND_DNRequiredA read-only service account of the directory.
LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_PASSWORD_FILENoneFile with its password, readable by the worker only.
LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_PASSWORDEmptyIts password, when LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_PASSWORD_FILE is not set.

A multi-valued LDAP attribute gives its first value. A user who leaves the directory, or loses an LDAP attribute, loses the value. A search that finds no user while values exist is refused, not applied, so that a wrong filter or base DN cannot remove every value at once; the values then become stale.

Files and logs of the access policy worker

FileAccess
CONSOLE_HTMLRead at startup: the model functions are extracted from it.

LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_CA_FILE, LDAP_ATTRIBUTES_PASSWORD_FILERead, with the LDAP attribute import.

One JSON object per line on standard output: {"time": "<ISO time>", "worker": "<host>-<pid>", "message": "...", ...}, for example started, reconciled (with the deployment ID, the result, the number of changes, and the keys that failed), and cycle failed. With --once, a failed cycle sets the exit code to 1.

Token authenticator

utils/web-console/sso_authenticator.mjs is the HTTP authentication server of single sign-on. The ClickHouse server asks it to check the sign-ins of the users IDENTIFIED WITH http SERVER '<SSO_SERVER_NAME>'; it accepts the sign-in when the password is a valid access token of the provider for that user. Optionally, its user sync creates, changes, and drops those users from the members of the provider's groups. The HTTP contract, the checks, and the sync are in the token authenticator API.

Running the token authenticator

bash
SSO_ISSUER=https://keycloak.example.com/realms/clickhouse SSO_CLIENT_ID=clickhouse-console SSO_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:29700 \
node utils/web-console/sso_authenticator.mjs

With the tools image, the command is sso-authenticator. Only the ClickHouse server should reach it. The server points to it with undefined.

ArgumentMeaning
NoneListen on SSO_LISTEN, and run the user sync every SSO_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS when it is configured.
--check-configFetch the provider's keys, print the configuration as JSON (issuer, client ID, audience, user name claim, token type, number of keys, and the sync settings or null), and exit.
--sync-onceRun one user sync, print each change on a line, and exit. Refused when the sync is not configured.

VariableDefaultMeaning

The sync is turned on by SSO_SYNC_CLIENT_ID or a secret, and then needs all of SSO_SYNC_CLIENT_ID, the secret, and CLICKHOUSE_USER.

Files, logs, and exit codes of the token authenticator

It reads SSO_SYNC_SECRET_FILE at startup, and writes nothing to disk. It logs one JSON object per line on standard output: {"time": "<ISO time>", "authenticator": "<host>-<pid>", "message": "...", ...}; the messages are listed in the token authenticator API.

ExitWhen
2A configuration error, printed as sso_authenticator: <message> on standard error: SSO_ISSUER or SSO_CLIENT_ID missing, a URL that is not HTTPS, an invalid SSO_SERVER_NAME, ADMIN_DATABASE, or role in SSO_DEFAULT_ROLES, an incomplete sync configuration, or --sync-once without a sync.
0--check-config or --sync-once finished.

Recovery rehearsal

utils/web-console/recovery_rehearsal.mjs proves that a whole server can be recovered from its backups, and from a staged server bundle when one is given, on an isolated server that it starts for the rehearsal and removes after it. Production is only read, and receives the result. The rehearsal server:

  • listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on its own ports, with its own data directory and embedded Keeper;
  • starts from the staged configuration with --staged, with the storage, Keeper, clusters, named collections storage, openSSL section, and paths replaced, so that it cannot write to production;
  • restores each backup from its real destination, which it only reads, into its own disk (storage_policy = 'default', allow_non_empty_tables = 0);
  • compares every table that has recorded values: the row count and the fingerprint (groupBitXor(cityHash64(*))).

The result is recorded as a check event named rehearsal of each backup (Recovery rehearsed in the inventory) and as a recovery_rehearsal audit record. See Recover a server.

Running the recovery rehearsal

bash
node utils/web-console/recovery_rehearsal.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:8123 --user <admin> --password <password> \
    --binary /usr/bin/clickhouse [--staged <staging directory of a server bundle>]

Run it on the server host, or on a host that mounts the backups: a disk destination is read from its path on this host.

ArgumentDefaultMeaning

--password <password>CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, or emptyIts password.
--backup <operation ID>The latest successful backup of each databaseA backup to rehearse; repeat for several.

--keepOffKeep the work directory at the end.

The work directory holds config/ (the configuration, with config.d/zz-rehearsal.xml and users.d/zz-rehearsal.xml for a user rehearsal with a random password), data/, server.log, and server.err.log. It is removed at the end, unless --keep is given.

The rehearsal prints progress lines as [HH:MM:SS] <message> on standard output, and ends with Recovery rehearsal: <n> of <m> backups restored and matched, or Recovery rehearsal failed: <reason>.

reference/token-authenticator-api.title: Token authenticator API
reference/token-authenticator-api.description: The HTTP contract between the ClickHouse server and the token authenticator of single sign-on: the request, the responses, the health check, every token check, the user sync, and the log format.
reference/token-authenticator-api.html:
This build of ClickHouse does not verify OpenID Connect tokens itself. It asks an HTTP authentication server to check the sign-ins of users IDENTIFIED WITH http SERVER '<name>' (see HTTP authentication). With single sign-on, the console sends the provider's access token as the password, and the token authenticator, utils/web-console/sso_authenticator.mjs, checks it. This page describes the contract between the server and the authenticator, as implemented by HTTPBasicAuthClient and SettingsAuthResponseParser (src/Access/) on the server side and by sso_authenticator.mjs on the other. For running the authenticator, see Helper processes.

text
Browser ──(X-ClickHouse-User: <user>, X-ClickHouse-Key: <access token>)──▶ ClickHouse server
ClickHouse server ──(GET, Authorization: Basic <user>:<access token>)──▶ token authenticator ──▶ provider's keys (JWKS)

Request

For each authentication of a user IDENTIFIED WITH http SERVER '<name>', the server sends one request to the uri of http_authentication_servers.<name> (see Configuration). Over the HTTP interface, every request of the user is authenticated, so the console causes one call per query.

PartValue
MethodGET
PathThe path and query of uri, for example /.
ProtocolHTTP/1.1
AuthorizationBasic with base64(<user name>:<password>): the user name of the sign-in, and the access token as the password.
Forwarded headersEach header of the client's request whose name is listed in forward_headers (names compared without case). A value with CR, LF, or NUL makes the sign-in fail with BAD_ARGUMENTS before any request is sent.
BodyNone

The server uses the timeouts of the configuration, and tries at most max_tries times. Only an exception while sending or receiving is retried, after retry_initial_backoff_ms, doubling up to retry_max_backoff_ms; when the last attempt fails, the sign-in fails. Any HTTP answer is final.

Responses

The server accepts the sign-in when, and only when, the status is 200 OK. With 200, it reads the body as JSON: when the body is an object with a key settings whose value is an object, each member is a setting applied to the session of the user, for example:

json
{"settings": {"max_execution_time": "60", "readonly": "1"}}

A body that is not valid JSON, or has no settings object, is ignored: the sign-in is still accepted. On a parse error the server logs Failed to parse settings from authentication response. Skip it. (logger HTTPAuthentication, level Information). Any other status refuses the sign-in.

The token authenticator answers every request with Content-Type: application/json and Cache-Control: no-store:

StatusBodyWhen
200{}The token is accepted for the user. The authenticator returns no settings.
401{}No Authorization: Basic header with a user:password pair, or the token fails a check.
405{}The method is not GET.
503{}The provider's keys cannot be fetched: the token cannot be checked, so the sign-in is refused (fail closed).

GET /health

A GET request to exactly /health is not a sign-in. It answers:

StatusBodyWhen
200{"keys": <number of keys>, "issuer": "<SSO_ISSUER>"}The provider's keys are loaded.
503The same, with "keys": 0No key is loaded yet.

Checks

The authenticator checks the token in this order, and refuses at the first check that fails. The refusal is answered with 401 and logged with the message refused, the user, and the reason below. The token itself is never logged.

#CheckReason logged
1The token has three parts separated by ..not a signed JWT
2The header and the payload are base64url-encoded JSON.malformed token
3The algorithm alg of the header is RS256, PS256, or ES256. A token signed with none or with a shared secret is refused.algorithm <alg> is not accepted
4The provider has a signing key with the key ID kid of the header. For an unknown key ID, the keys are fetched again, at most every 30 seconds, because the provider may have rotated them.unknown key <kid>
5When the key names an algorithm, it is the algorithm of the header.key <kid> is for <key alg>, not <alg>
6The signature is valid for that key (SHA-256).invalid signature
7The claim iss is SSO_ISSUER.issuer <iss>
8Unless SSO_TOKEN_TYPE is empty, the claim typ is SSO_TOKEN_TYPE (default Bearer): an access token, not an ID token.token type <typ>, not an access token
9The claim azp is SSO_CLIENT_ID.issued to <azp>, not <SSO_CLIENT_ID>
10Unless SSO_AUDIENCE is empty, the claim aud (a string or an array) includes SSO_AUDIENCE (default SSO_CLIENT_ID).audience does not include <SSO_AUDIENCE>
11The claim exp is a number, and exp plus 30 seconds is not in the past.expired
12When the claim nbf is a number, nbf minus 30 seconds is not in the future.not valid yet
13When the claim iat is a number, iat minus 30 seconds is not in the future.issued in the future
14The claim SSO_USERNAME_CLAIM (default preferred_username) is exactly the user name of the sign-in.the claim <SSO_USERNAME_CLAIM> is not the user name

When the keys cannot be fetched during check 4, the answer is 503, logged as cannot check the token with the user and the error.

The provider's keys

The keys come from the discovery document <SSO_ISSUER>/.well-known/openid-configuration:

  • the document's issuer must be SSO_ISSUER;
  • its jwks_uri and token_endpoint must use HTTPS, or HTTP on localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1]; otherwise the authenticator stops with exit code 2;
  • of the JSON Web Key Set, only keys with a kid and with use sig (or no use) are kept; a key that cannot be read is skipped and logged as skipped a key the authenticator cannot read.

The keys are loaded at startup. When they cannot be loaded then, the authenticator logs cannot load the keys of the provider yet and starts anyway; each sign-in tries to load them again, and is refused with 503 until it succeeds.

A token is accepted until it expires. The console refreshes it while the user is signed in; a user disabled in the provider can no longer refresh, so access ends at the latest when the last token expires (5 minutes by default in Keycloak).

User sync

With SSO_SYNC_CLIENT_ID, the secret, and CLICKHOUSE_USER, the authenticator keeps the users of single sign-on in line with the provider every SSO_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 60), and once at startup. It changes only users identified with this authentication server, never a user with a password or another authentication method.

Calls to the provider

The calls use the Keycloak admin API, whose base is the issuer with /realms/<realm> replaced by /admin/realms/<realm>:

#RequestPurpose
1POST <token_endpoint>, form grant_type=client_credentials, client_id=<SSO_SYNC_CLIENT_ID>, client_secret=<secret>An access token of the service account.
2GET <admin base>/groups?search=<SSO_ROLE_PREFIX>&briefRepresentation=true&max=1000, with Authorization: Bearer <token>The groups, with their subgroups. Only groups whose name starts with SSO_ROLE_PREFIX are used.
3GET <admin base>/groups/<group id>/members?first=<offset>&max=500&briefRepresentation=true for each such group, paged by 500The members.

The service account needs the roles view-users and query-groups of the client realm-management. The provider requests time out after 15 seconds (5 seconds for the token request).

A group <SSO_ROLE_PREFIX><role> gives the role <role>. Members that are not enabled are skipped. The user name of a member is its username when SSO_USERNAME_CLAIM is preferred_username, otherwise the member's attribute of that name, or its username when it has none. Each member gets the roles of all its groups and SSO_DEFAULT_ROLES.

Reads from ClickHouse

QueryPurpose
SELECT u.name, groupArrayIf(g.granted_role_name, ...) FROM system.users AS u LEFT JOIN system.role_grants AS g ... WHERE has(u.auth_type, 'http') GROUP BY u.nameUsers with HTTP authentication, and their granted roles.
SHOW CREATE USER <name> for eachKeeps only users whose statement contains IDENTIFIED WITH http SERVER '<SSO_SERVER_NAME>': system.users does not show the server of an HTTP user.
SELECT name FROM system.rolesThe roles that exist.
SELECT name FROM system.usersAll users, to detect a name taken by another authentication method.

Safety check

When the provider shows no group with the prefix while users identified with this server exist, the sync is refused and nothing is changed: a wrong prefix, a wrong realm, or a service account that cannot see the groups must not remove every user at once. The error is logged as sync failed. Groups whose members all left are a valid answer and do remove those users.

Changes

For each member, in order:

ConditionStatementAudit action
A role it would get does not existNone: the role is skipped, logged as roles that do not exist are skipped.—
A user of that name exists with another authentication methodNone: the member is skipped, logged as a user of that name exists with another authentication: skipped.—
No user of that name existsCREATE USER `<user>` IDENTIFIED WITH http SERVER '<SSO_SERVER_NAME>' SCHEME 'BASIC'sso_create_user
It should have roles it does not haveGRANT `<role>`, ... TO `<user>` sso_grant_roles
It has roles it should not haveREVOKE `<role>`, ... FROM `<user>` sso_revoke_roles
Roles were granted or revokedSET DEFAULT ROLE ALL TO `<user>` sso_default_roles

Then, for each user identified with this server that is no longer a member of a prefixed group, or is disabled or deleted in the provider: DROP USER `<user>` , audit action sso_drop_user.

The roles compared are all roles granted to the user, so a role granted to a user of single sign-on outside the sync is revoked at the next sync. Statements run one after another; a failing statement is logged as sync statement failed and audited with failure, and the sync continues with the next one. At the end it logs users synced with the number of members and of changes.

Audit records

Unless ADMIN_DATABASE is empty, each statement is recorded in <ADMIN_DATABASE>.audit_log:

ColumnValue
correlation_idA new UUID per statement.
scopelocal
target_typeuser
target_nameThe user name.
actionsso_create_user, sso_grant_roles, sso_revoke_roles, sso_default_roles, or sso_drop_user.
summaryFor example Create the SSO user <user>, Grant <roles> to <user>, Revoke <roles> from <user>, Enable every role of <user> by default, or Drop the SSO user <user>: no longer in a <prefix>* group, or disabled.
resultsuccess or failure.
errorThe error of a failed statement.
details{"by": "sso_authenticator", "server": "<SSO_SERVER_NAME>"}

The actor of the records is the sync's account (CLICKHOUSE_USER). When a record cannot be written, the authenticator logs the audit record could not be written and continues.

Log format

The authenticator writes one JSON object per line on standard output:

json
{"time": "2026-11-12T10:00:00.000Z", "authenticator": "<host name>-<process ID>", "message": "refused", "user": "kara", "reason": "expired"}
MessageFieldsWhen
keys loadedissuer, keysAt startup, when the keys were loaded.
cannot load the keys of the provider yeterrorAt startup, when they could not be loaded.
listeningaddress, client_id, syncThe HTTP server listens.
skipped a key the authenticator cannot readkid, errorA key of the JSON Web Key Set cannot be used.
refuseduser, reasonA sign-in was refused; see Checks.
cannot check the tokenuser, errorThe keys could not be fetched; answered 503.
roles that do not exist are skippeduser, rolesSync.
a user of that name exists with another authentication: skippeduserSync.
sync statement faileduser, errorSync.
the audit record could not be writtenaction, target, errorSync.
users syncedmembers, changesEnd of a sync.
sync failederrorA sync was refused or failed.

Accepted sign-ins are not logged. Configuration errors are printed to standard error as sso_authenticator: <message>, and the process exits with code 2.
